title: Preserve speaker and addressee attribution in recent_hearing, cues.dialogue, and memory retrieval

sections.what: Preserve `speaker` and optional `target`/`addressed_to` attribution from `recent_hearing` through `memory-context.ts` into `engine/memory_retrieval.py` so associative recall knows who said what and to whom.
sections.why: `engine/speech.py` already stores `speaker` (and `whisper_target` on whispers) inside `recent_hearing`, yet `memory-context.ts` strips `h.speaker` before calling `retrievePlayerMemories`, and `engine/memory_retrieval.py` flattens all `dialogue` lines into an unattributed token set. Identical remarks from completely different relationships (e.g. playful teasing from a crush vs predatory harassment from an antagonist) hash to the same cue tokens.
sections.how: 1. Add optional `addressed_to` / `target` recording on public speech events in `engine/speech.py` so `recent_hearing` entries keep both `speaker` and `target` cleanly.\n2. Update `static/js/agent/prompt-builder/memory-context.ts` (`heardLines` / `dialogueLines`) to build structured `{ speaker, target, text }` dialogue cue entries (keeping legacy string support for backward-compatible callers) instead of dropping `h.speaker`.\n3. Update `engine/memory_retrieval.py` (`extract_cues`, `score_memory`) so attributed dialogue extracts speaker/target actor cues and evaluates `(speaker + content)` binding cleanly without falsely boosting unrelated actors' quotes that happen to share words.
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest retrieval tests where Memory A and Memory B share identical quoted words from different speakers/addressees, asserting speaker-matched recall beats unattributed token overlap.\n2. Run JS unit tests for `PromptBuilder.buildMemoryContext` verifying `retrievePlayerMemories` receives structured speaker-attributed `dialogue` entries, then run `npm run build:ts`.

acceptance.text: Public directed speech records optional addressee/target metadata on `recent_hearing` entries in `engine/speech.py` alongside `speaker` (parity with `whisper_target` on whispers).
`static/js/agent/prompt-builder/memory-context.ts` preserves `{ speaker, target, text }` attribution on `cues.dialogue` (and structured `stimulus`) instead of stripping `h.speaker`.

`engine/memory_retrieval.py` (`extract_cues` and Channel 2/3 scoring) distinguishes who said a line and to whom when matching memories, preventing identical words from different speakers from collapsing onto the wrong person's memory.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Agent Lens (`static/js/agent-lens.ts`) and Mind / Memory retrieval debug payloads via `routes/memories.py`.

Current availability: `engine/speech.py` stores `speaker` on `recent_hearing` entries, while `memory-context.ts` drops `h.speaker` before calling `/memories/retrieve`.

Why no new UI panel: Fixes perceptual cue serialization between `speech.py`, `memory-context.ts`, and `engine/memory_retrieval.py`; surfaced automatically in Agent Lens memory scoring details.

Manual verification steps:
1. Trigger two memories with similar dialogue phrasing from two different speakers (e.g. an affectionate friend vs a hostile acquaintance) and have one speaker talk in the current scene.
2. Open Agent Lens or inspect the `explain: true` payload from `/memories/retrieve`.
   - expected: `cues` carries attributed `{ speaker, target, text }` dialogue items and retrieval scores prefer memories bound to the actual speaker/addressee.
